thread:
elaine: Quick heads-up — found an access edgecase in Console. Viewer users are able to trigger a deployment rollback when the project has the legacy feature-flag 'allow-operator:true'. Repro in staging. filing as potential P0 since it escalates privileges.

samir: ack, can you paste the minimal repro steps and the API call you saw?

elaine: steps:
1) create project with legacy flag set
2) invite user with role Viewer
3) go to Deployments -> select active deployment
4) UI shows 'Rollback' action on the kebab menu
5) click -> POST /api/v1/deployments/<id>/rollback -> 202 returned

samir: that sounds like UI gating bug — backend should enforce permission but we rely on middleware that reads new roles. maybe old flag bypasses check.

jordan: are the RBAC checks using the role matrix service or the old inline perms? @samir any idea which codepath handles rollback?

samir: rollback uses deployments.controller -> actions.go -> performRollback, which calls auth.CanPerform(user, resource, action). The auth layer has two implementations: role-matrix and legacy-allowlist. feature flag 'allow-operator' is toggled in the middleware to use legacy path for backwards compat. I think the legacy path incorrectly maps Viewer -> operator in one mapping table.

ajay: if viewers can trigger rollback, KMS decrypt actions might also be accessible (rollback touches image keys). We need to check KMS audit logs for any decrypts by viewer accounts in prod/staging.

security-bot: automatically created incident INC-2026 when keyword 'P0' present. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rbac-incident

elaine: I checked staging KMS logs: no decrypts from the viewer user yet — looks limited to rollback orchestration which queues a task that later requests KMS. In staging, queue worker used service account, not user creds. But still breach of intent.

ops-oncall: suggest immediate mitigation: flip UI flag to hide rollback button for projects with legacy flag OR temporarily block legacy flag usage. Which is faster?

samir: fastest: return 403 from performRollback if user role < Editor. I'll open a quick PR to add explicit server-side guard. UI hide is nicer but not sufficient.

ajay: agree — server-side guard first. also we should add an audit event for attempted rollbacks with actor role and project flag state. Right now audit logs only record success, not attempted/denied actions for that endpoint.

elaine: filing tickets:
- P0: server guard for rollback (samir)
- P1: add audit event for attempted/denied rollback (ajay)
- P1: remove legacy auto-mapping or add explicit mapping review (jordan)
- P2: run KMS decrypt scan for prod/staging in last 30d (security)

samir: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/5831 — adds auth.CanPerform check returning 403 early and unit tests. cc @elaine for repro test.

jordan: also add an integration test that provisions a project with 'allow-operator:true' and ensures Viewer cannot call rollback API.

elaine: will validate in staging once PR merges. also adding note to customer-impact doc in case any customers used legacy flag.

ops-oncall: if we see any similar endpoints where legacy path bypasses role-matrix, we should consider a global feature-flag quarantine. but start small.

ajay: I'll add the audit-change ticket and a small schema for "attempted_action" events: actor, role_at_time, action, resource, flag_state, outcome.

security-bot: reminder: include CVE-style id if this turns into externally reportable vuln. use security triage template: https://redwood.internal/security/triage

elaine: thanks team. tagging @samir @ajay @jordan. will post follow-up after staging validation :thumbsup:

samir: merged and deploying to staging now. will update when validated.

elaine: validated — viewer no longer can hit rollback API, audit shows denied attempt logged. moving to monitoring. closing P0 once it lands in prod.
